newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH LEAGUE MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: The following matches are being played in the Spanish first division this weekend (league positions in parentheses, all kickoff times GMT)
With only one defeat away this season Racing could pose a threat to an Atletico side that looks like title material again after the reappearance of Jose Luis Caminero.
With Davor Suker in fine form new leaders Real Madrid hope to maintain their good record at Sporting, where former Real coach Benito Floro has come under heavy fire.
New coach Jorge Valdano has been forced by injury problems to change the Valencia defence for his home debut against a Celta side that has hit form after a weak start.
Rayo Vallecano were boosted by a 5-1 cup win over Albacete on Wednesday and will be looking for their first win in the top flight at Tenerife, who have been hit by injuries.
Sevilla's Brazilian star Bebeto is struggling to get fit for the game against his old club, who are looking for only their third victory in the Sanchez Pizjuan stadium in 25 visits.
With just a third of the championship gone, the situation is already looking desperate for both of these sides in a season in which four teams face automatic relegation.
Alfonso Perez hopes to celebrate his 50th game for a Betis side unbeaten away from home and looking to win in Galicia for the third year in a row to stay in touch at the top.
Victor Esparrago will be without defender Quique Sanchez as Zaragoza aim for their first home league win after a week in which both sides thrashed weaker teams in the cup.
Unexpectedly dumped out of the Spanish Cup on Wednesday, Real Sociedad hope to bounce back against an Espanyol side still trying to recapture last season's form.
A game seen as the clash of two managers -- Athletic's hyperactive Luis Fernandez and Valladolid's laid-back Victor Cantatore -- both of whom have surprised their critics.
With Josep Guardiola and Sergi Barjuan suspended, Barcelona give a chance to Ivan de la Pena in a David-Goliath clash against the bottom club, who are yet to win away.
